opportunities.name: Browser Upload Bridge
opportunities.title: Hidden file-input fallback for agent browsers
opportunities.thesis: Agents still hit browser flows where the native file chooser never fires. Ship a tiny browser/MCP bridge that can target hidden file inputs directly and hand the agent a deterministic upload primitive.
opportunities.signal: Recent Codex request closed as not planned; the underlying Playwright primitive already exists.
opportunities.move: Wrap setInputFiles behind one safe tool + demo it against 5 common upload flows.

opportunities.name: Codex KeepWarm
opportunities.title: Tool calls stall after idle gaps on Windows
opportunities.thesis: If idle transitions are the trigger, a tiny watchdog/keepalive sidecar may remove minutes of dead time without changing Codex itself.
opportunities.signal: September blocker report; every post-idle tool call reportedly incurs ~30s latency and upstream closed it as not planned.
opportunities.move: Reproduce, then test whether a low-cost heartbeat prevents the stall. Kill immediately if it does not.

opportunities.name: Goalkeeper
opportunities.title: Persist goals across codex exec sessions
opportunities.thesis: A wrapper can own the durable goal, inject it into new/resumed runs, and expose goal state programmatically without waiting for first-class CLI support.
opportunities.signal: Two closely related programmatic-goal requests were closed as not planned.
opportunities.move: Build codex-goal with set/show/run; dogfood it on a multi-run task.

opportunities.name: Context Curator
opportunities.title: Scoped compaction for exploratory phases
opportunities.thesis: Treat transcripts as editable context: preserve conclusions, compress dead ends, and emit a clean continuation packet for the next agent/session.
opportunities.signal: Users explicitly want selective rather than whole-history compaction; Claude Code users are asking for priority-aware compaction too.
opportunities.move: Take a real long transcript, select one noisy span, produce a resumable compacted version, measure token savings.

opportunities.name: Finishline
opportunities.title: The project-management layer coding agents are missing
opportunities.thesis: External supervisor that tracks objective → evidence → acceptance, catches unfinished work, and refuses to equate agent completion with done.
opportunities.signal: The request is unusually explicit about sprawl, verification, multi-tier workflow, and agents claiming completion without evidence.
opportunities.move: Ship a repo-local supervisor card that reads task + git state + acceptance checks and produces DONE/WAIT/ANDON.

opportunities.name: Preview Sidecar
opportunities.title: Bring back local preview for agent-built apps
opportunities.thesis: A tiny localhost/port discovery sidecar can surface the app the agent is building without requiring the coding product itself to own preview UX.
opportunities.signal: Users describe preview removal as a major regression and specifically want localhost surfaced again.
opportunities.move: Detect active localhost ports and expose one-click preview + screenshot receipt.

opportunities.name: Context Priority
opportunities.title: Let users mark low-priority context before compaction
opportunities.thesis: A context sidecar can assign priority to transcript segments and generate a compacted continuation packet that preserves high-value state first.
opportunities.signal: Same underlying pain as scoped compaction, now expressed as explicit message-level priority.
opportunities.move: Prototype priority annotations + deterministic compaction on exported sessions.

opportunities.name: Model Presets
opportunities.title: Named model + effort presets
opportunities.thesis: One-click named presets are externally solvable today with a wrapper/menu that atomically selects model and effort and persists the choice.
opportunities.signal: Current product exposes the pieces but not the composed action users want.
opportunities.move: Ship a 3-preset CLI/menu-bar prototype: fast / think / max.

opportunities.name: Browser Guardrail
opportunities.title: Per-task domain and form-submission constraints
opportunities.thesis: Put an authority layer in front of browser agents: task-scoped domains, submission policy, and receipts. The browser stays powerful; the delegation gets narrow.
opportunities.signal: The issue frames a real prompt-injection blast-radius problem and upstream closed the feature as not planned.
opportunities.move: Proxy three dangerous actions—navigate, fill, submit—through a task policy and prove denials are deterministic.
